result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.max_clique()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a maximum clique in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12281-L12363){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.max_clique() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Maximum clique](/assets/graphs/max-clique.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node graph. The triangle 2, 3, 5, in the accent color, is the largest set of nodes that are all pairwise connected. The card shows the result [2, 3, 5], size 3." width="100%"} A maximum clique is a largest possible clique in the graph. If multiple maximum cliques exist with the same size, returns one of them (arbitrary choice). Uses the Bron-Kerbosch algorithm to enumerate all maximal cliques and selects the largest. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted list of node IDs forming a maximum clique. Empty list if graph is empty. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on a directed graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Finding a maximum clique is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard and, in fact, inapproximable within any factor of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ unless $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$. This implementation enumerates all maximal cliques via Bron-Kerbosch and returns the largest, which inherits the algorithm's $O(3^{n/3})$ worst-case runtime but performs well on sparse and structured inputs. If more than one maximum clique exists, one is returned arbitrarily. Undirected graphs only. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a triangle, the maximum clique is the whole graph: ::: {#80f1f051 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) graph.max_clique() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [1, 2, 3] ``` ::: ::: In a path, no three nodes are mutually connected, so the maximum clique is just a single edge: ::: {#f07da7c7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) graph.max_clique() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [1, 2] ``` ::: ::: An empty graph has no clique to find: ::: {#451e8c73 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph(directed=False).max_clique() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [] ``` ::: ::: In a complete graph, the maximum clique is every node: ::: {#63bbce0c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=6) len(graph.max_clique()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
